root_cause: scc 4.1.0 counts the // line inside a Java raw-string literal (text block) as a comment even though it is raw-string content; this is a known scc limitation documented in tests/metrics/run.py
scc 4.1.0 counts the // line inside a C# raw-string literal as a comment even though it is raw-string content; this is a known scc limitation documented in tests/metrics/run.py

Standalone scc 4.1.0 maps .h files to its 'C Header' grammar, which counts #ifdef/#if/#elif/#else preprocessor branches as complexity contributions. dircue maps .h files via the Linguist language table to the 'C' grammar, which does not count those preprocessor branches as complexity. The code/comment/blank/lines counts agree; only complexity differs. The proposed --selection scc flag (#12) would align dircue's grammar selection with scc's.

Standalone scc 4.1.0 maps .tpl files to its 'Smarty Template' grammar. dircue maps .tpl files to 'Go Template' via the Linguist language table. The {{/* ... */}} comment syntax is recognized by Go Template grammar but not by Smarty Template grammar, so code/comment counts differ between the two tools for files using that comment form. The proposed --selection scc flag (#12) would align dircue's grammar selection with scc's.

Standalone scc 4.1.0 maps .t files to 'Raku' (Perl 6) by extension. dircue reads the shebang line and maps files starting with #!/bin/bash to 'Shell'. Raku and Shell grammars have different complexity-keyword sets, so complexity counts differ for shebang-identified shell scripts with a .t extension.
